vvi.topic: Interference, thin films and Newton's rings
vvi.note: Superposition of coherent waves gives maxima when the path difference is nλ and minima at (2n−1)λ/2. In reflected light a thin film adds λ/2 for the air-film boundary, so the condition flips. Newton's rings have radii proportional to √n, with a dark centre in reflected light.

vvi.topic: Diffraction and the diffraction grating
vvi.note: Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit has minima at a sin θ = nλ; a grating has principal maxima at d sin θ = nλ, with d the grating spacing. Resolving power of a grating is nN. Distinguish interference (few sources) from diffraction (continuous wavefront) when the question asks.

vvi.topic: Laser: population inversion, pumping and properties
vvi.note: Three ingredients: a gain medium with population inversion, a pump to create it, and an optical resonator for feedback. Emission is stimulated, so the output is coherent, monochromatic, directional and intense. Einstein's A and B coefficients relate spontaneous and stimulated emission.

vvi.topic: Optical fibre: numerical aperture and attenuation
vvi.note: Light is guided by total internal reflection when the core index exceeds the cladding index. NA = √(n₁² − n₂²) and the acceptance angle is sin⁻¹(NA). Attenuation is 10 log(Pin/Pout)/L dB/km; dispersion limits bandwidth.

vvi.topic: Rolle's theorem and Lagrange's mean value theorem
vvi.note: Rolle: if f is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b) and f(a) = f(b), some c has f'(c) = 0. Lagrange: some c has f'(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a). State the three conditions before proving, and use the theorem to bound a function or locate a root.

vvi.topic: Taylor and Maclaurin series expansions
vvi.note: f(x) = Σ f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)(x−a)ⁿ/n!; Maclaurin is the case a = 0. Memorise eˣ, sin x, cos x, log(1+x) and (1+x)ⁿ, then derive an unfamiliar expansion from one of them. State the remainder if the question asks for the error.

vvi.topic: Rank of a matrix and consistency of linear equations
vvi.note: Reduce to row-echelon form; rank is the number of non-zero rows. For AX = B compare rank(A) with rank([A|B]): equal to the number of unknowns gives a unique solution, equal but smaller gives infinitely many, and rank(A) < rank([A|B]) means inconsistent. Also compute rank from the largest non-zero minor.

vvi.topic: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix
vvi.note: Solve |A − λI| = 0 for eigenvalues, then (A − λI)X = 0 for eigenvectors. The sum of eigenvalues equals the trace and their product equals the determinant. For a symmetric matrix, eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.

vvi.topic: Partial derivatives and Euler's theorem on homogeneous functions
vvi.note: For a homogeneous function of degree n, x·∂u/∂x + y·∂u/∂y = n·u. Check homogeneity by replacing x with tx and y with ty: u(tx,ty) = tⁿu(x,y). Chain rule for composite functions is the other standard question.

vvi.topic: Beta and Gamma functions
vvi.note: Γ(n) = (n−1)! for a positive integer, Γ(1/2) = √π, and B(m,n) = Γ(m)Γ(n)/Γ(m+n). Use the relation to evaluate definite integrals that match the Beta form ∫₀¹ x^(m−1)(1−x)^(n−1) dx.

vvi.topic: Data types, operators and type conversion in C
vvi.note: int, float, double, char and their sizes; % for integers gives the remainder and / truncates integer division. Implicit promotion goes to the wider type; cast explicitly with (float). Know operator precedence: *, /, % before +, −, and = last.

vvi.topic: Control flow: if-else, switch and loops
vvi.note: switch works on integer or char constants and needs break to avoid fall-through. for is used when the count is known, while when it is not, do-while when the body must run at least once. Every loop needs an exit condition that the body actually changes.

vvi.topic: Arrays and strings in C
vvi.note: An array is a contiguous block, indexed from 0; passing it to a function passes a pointer, so the size must be passed too. A C string is a char array ending in '\0'; use strlen, strcpy, strcat and strcmp from string.h. A bubble sort or matrix addition trace is the usual program.

vvi.topic: Functions, call by value and recursion
vvi.note: C is call by value only: the callee gets copies, so a function that must change a variable takes its address. A recursive function needs a base case and a step that moves toward it; write the factorial and Fibonacci traces with stack frames.

vvi.topic: Pointers and pointer arithmetic
vvi.note: A pointer stores an address; * dereferences and & takes an address. p + 1 advances by sizeof(*p), not one byte. Arrays decay to pointers, so a[i] equals *(a + i). Use pointers for out-parameters and dynamic memory (malloc/free).

vvi.topic: Structures, unions and typedef
vvi.note: A structure holds members of different types; a union overlays them in one block sized by the largest member. Access with . or ->, typedef names the type, and an array of structures stores records. Structure padding means sizeof(struct) may exceed the sum of members.

vvi.topic: KVL, KCL and mesh or nodal analysis
vvi.note: KCL: the sum of currents at a node is zero; KVL: the sum of voltages around a loop is zero. Mesh analysis writes KVL for each independent loop, nodal analysis writes KCL at each independent node. Pick one and solve the linear system; state the assumed current directions.

vvi.topic: Thevenin's and Norton's theorems
vvi.note: Thevenin replaces a linear network by Vth in series with Rth; Norton by In in parallel with Rn, where Vth = In·Rn and Rth = Rn. Find Vth as the open-circuit voltage, In as the short-circuit current, and Rth by killing the sources and looking in. Maximum power transfer needs RL = Rth.

vvi.topic: Single-phase AC circuits and power factor
vvi.note: XL = 2πfL and XC = 1/(2πfC); impedance Z = R + j(XL − XC). At resonance XL = XC, Z is purely resistive and the power factor is unity. Real power P = VI cos φ, reactive Q = VI sin φ, apparent S = VI; draw the phasor diagram.

vvi.topic: Transformers: EMF equation, losses and efficiency
vvi.note: E = 4.44 f N Φm, so the turns ratio sets the voltage ratio. Core loss (hysteresis and eddy current) is constant with load; copper loss varies as I²R. Efficiency = output/(output + core + copper), maximum when copper loss equals core loss. An ideal transformer has no losses and no leakage.

vvi.topic: Carpentry: tools and joints
vvi.note: Carpentry holds wood with joints rather than fasteners: mortise and tenon for frames, dovetail for drawers, halving and bridle joints for cheaper work. Marking uses a try square, steel rule and mortise gauge; the tenon saw and chisel cut the joint and a plane trues the face. Name the tools with the joint when the question asks for a sketch.

vvi.topic: Fitting: bench tools, limits and fits
vvi.note: Fitting brings a metal part to size by hand: a hacksaw cuts, files remove the last half millimetre, and a scraper or reamer finishes. A vernier caliper or micrometer checks the size against the drawing. Limits give the permitted maximum and minimum size, and clearance, interference and transition fits describe the resulting assembly.

vvi.topic: Arc welding and its defects
vvi.note: An electric arc between the electrode and the work melts both; the flux coating shields the pool and forms slag that is chipped off afterwards. DCEN puts more heat at the work and gives deeper penetration, DCEP puts more heat at the electrode. Slag inclusion, porosity, undercut, lack of penetration, distortion and cracks are the defects to name with their cause.

vvi.topic: Lathe operations and cutting parameters
vvi.note: The lathe turns a rotating workpiece against a single-point tool fed along the bed. Facing, plain and step turning, taper turning with the compound rest, thread cutting with the half-nut, knurling and drilling from the tailstock are the standard operations. Cutting speed is πDN/1000 m/min and feed is mm per revolution.

vvi.topic: Least count of vernier caliper and micrometer
vvi.note: Least count is the smallest value an instrument can read: for a vernier caliper it is 1 MSD − 1 VSD, which is 0.02 mm with 50 divisions, and for a micrometer it is pitch divided by thimble divisions, which is 0.01 mm. The reading is the main-scale value plus the coinciding division times the least count, with the zero error added or subtracted.
